primary_sources.cite: Dungan & Chang, Proc R Soc B 2017, doi:10.1098/rspb.2016.2743

structures.notes: Bovine, dark-state 11-cis retinal, numbering equals UniProt and equals human. All named residues present. Ala292 and Gly121 are 3.3 A and 3.7 A from retinal and 10.3 A apart.

known_limitations: Retinal-release after photoactivation is not a direct dark-noise rate; do not treat the white paper's dark-noise mechanism as measured here.
Teleosts are absent from the mammal-only TOGA2 alignment, as is Rhinolophus unihastatus. Cetaceans (75) and bats (113) are well represented.
1U19 is the dark state; any claim about transducin coupling needs an active-state structure, which is not in the repo.
RH3's ordering has no local experimental source.
expected_outcome_note: RH1 is the single best epistasis ground truth in the whole white paper: a published, statistically tested background dependence. Weight it heavily.

replication_targets.finding: Site 83 has a significant effect on the measured phenotype, and its effect differs between species backgrounds (significant species-by-site interaction).
replication_targets.source: Dungan & Chang 2017 supplement, Supplementary Table 1 two-way ANOVA
replication_targets.test: This is a genuine published epistasis result. Does epistaeon detect site 83 as background-dependent?

replication_targets.finding: Sites 83, 292 and 299 are the assayed positions.

white_paper_claims_not_in_source.finding: The white paper claims permissive transmembrane substitutions (G121L, E122Q) rigidified the pocket before spectral tuning (D83N, A292S).
white_paper_claims_not_in_source.test: Ordering claim. Check whether any local source supports it; Yokoyama's ancestral rhodopsin supplement was not obtainable.

authority_rule: The original study is the sole authority for what counts as a replication target. Claims in white_paper_claims_not_in_source have no published source in the local materials; epistaeon must NOT be scored against them. Record what epistaeon says about them for information only, and never count a mismatch as an epistaeon failure.
